A balanced scale scale with "Assets" on the left plate and "Capital + Liabilities" on the right plate. Below it, a flowchart pointing to a Statement of Financial Position, categorising Assets into 'Non-Current' and 'Current', and Capital/Liabilities into 'Capital', 'Long-term Liabilities', and 'Current Liabilities'. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A horizontal timeline representing a financial year from 1 January to 31 December. An arrow pointing past 31 December is labelled 'Prepayment (paid for next year, subtract from expense, Current Asset)'. An arrow pointing just before 31 December with a gap to the end is labelled 'Accrual (used this year but not paid, add to expense, Current Liability)'. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A line graph comparing straight-line and reducing balance depreciation over 5 years. The X-axis represents 'Years' from 0 to 5. The Y-axis represents 'Net Book Value (₦)'. The straight-line method is shown as a steady straight downward-sloping line. The reducing balance method is shown as a curve that drops steeply at first and then flattens out, never quite reaching zero.
